title: Liver biopsy
what: Through a puncture in your right side, the doctor uses a thin needle to take a tiny piece of liver for testing. It is done with local numbing and ultrasound guidance.
why: To find the cause of liver disease, to see how much the liver has changed, or to check a growth in the liver.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 15 to 30 minutes, then a few hours of observation; results usually in 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will decide if anything needs to change

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before a biopsy, blood clotting and platelets are always checked.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 6 to 8 hours before. The clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Your day
prepare.text: Keep the whole day free. After the biopsy, you need to lie down for a few hours under observation.

bring: Your referral, tests, and ultrasound, CT, or MRI images
steps: An IV line is put in a vein
You lie on your back with your right arm behind your head
The doctor chooses a spot on your right side using ultrasound
The skin is cleaned and numbed with an injection
You are asked to breathe out and hold your breath for a few seconds
A tiny piece of tissue is quickly taken with a thin needle
A bandage is put on, and you lie on your right side
feel: A prick and stinging from the numbing
A click and brief pressure as the tissue is taken
Afterward, your side or right shoulder may ache. That is normal
after: You lie down for a few hours while you are watched and your blood pressure is checked
No lifting or sports for 24 hours, and no heavy exertion for a week. Ask your doctor
The bandage comes off the next day
Your doctor usually explains the results at a visit
red_flags: Severe belly or side pain that keeps getting worse: call emergency services
Dizziness, weakness, a fast pulse, or cold sweat: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or shortness of breath

faq.q: Why does my shoulder hurt after a liver biopsy?
faq.a: It is referred pain from a nerve near the liver. It usually goes away in 1 to 2 days.

faq.q: Why do I need to hold my breath?
faq.a: The liver moves when you breathe. Holding your breath helps take the tissue accurately and safely.

reminders.text: Liver biopsy tomorrow. Do not eat after the time your clinic gave you. Keep the whole day free and bring someone with you.
